<section id="calculator" class="j2-rc-calc" aria-labelledby="calc-title">
<h2 id="calc-title">Fee calculator</h2>
<p class="j2-rc-lead">Choose a race, the number of runners and the number of T-shirts. The total updates as you go.</p>
<div class="j2-rc-layout">
  <div class="j2-rc-panel" role="group" aria-labelledby="calc-title">
    <label for="calc-race">Race</label>
    <select id="calc-race">
      <option value="5k" data-name="5K" selected>5K (Rs 300)</option>
      <option value="10k" data-name="10K">10K (Rs 500)</option>
      <option value="half" data-name="Half Marathon">Half Marathon (Rs 800)</option>
    </select>
    <label for="calc-runners">Number of runners (1 to 10)</label>
    <input id="calc-runners" type="number" inputmode="numeric" min="1" max="10" step="1" value="1">
    <label for="calc-shirts">Number of T-shirts (Rs 250 each, optional)</label>
    <input id="calc-shirts" type="number" inputmode="numeric" min="0" step="1" value="0">
    <label class="j2-rc-early" for="calc-early">
      <input id="calc-early" type="checkbox">
      <span>Early-bird: registering on or before 31 December 2026</span>
    </label>
    <p class="j2-rc-note" id="calc-early-note">Early-bird applies up to 31 December 2026: 10% off race fees only, never on T-shirts.</p>
    <p class="j2-rc-msg" id="calc-msg" role="alert"></p>
  </div>
  <div class="j2-rc-result" aria-live="polite">
    <h3>Your cost</h3>
    <dl class="j2-rc-rows">
      <div class="j2-rc-row"><dt id="calc-race-label">Race fees</dt><dd id="calc-race-amt">Rs 300</dd></div>
      <div class="j2-rc-row" id="calc-disc-row" hidden><dt>Early-bird 10% off race fees</dt><dd id="calc-disc-amt">- Rs 0</dd></div>
      <div class="j2-rc-row"><dt id="calc-shirt-label">T-shirts (no discount)</dt><dd id="calc-shirt-amt">Rs 0</dd></div>
    </dl>
    <p class="j2-rc-total-label">Total</p>
    <output id="calc-total" class="j2-rc-total" for="calc-race calc-runners calc-shirts calc-early">Rs 300</output>
    <a class="j2-btn j2-btn-secondary" href="#register">Continue to registration</a>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var FEES = { '5k': 300, '10k': 500, 'half': 800 };
  var SHIRT = 250;
  var MAX_RUNNERS = 10;
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var race = $('calc-race'), runners = $('calc-runners'), shirts = $('calc-shirts');
  var early = $('calc-early'), total = $('calc-total'), msg = $('calc-msg'), note = $('calc-early-note');
  var raceLabel = $('calc-race-label'), raceAmt = $('calc-race-amt');
  var discRow = $('calc-disc-row'), discAmt = $('calc-disc-amt');
  var shirtLabel = $('calc-shirt-label'), shirtAmt = $('calc-shirt-amt');
  if (!race || !runners || !shirts || !early || !total) { return; }

  function money(n) { return 'Rs ' + n.toLocaleString('en-IN'); }
  function toInt(v) {
    var s = String(v).replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, '');
    return /^\d+$/.test(s) ? parseInt(s, 10) : NaN;
  }
  function setText(el, t) { if (el) { el.textContent = t; } }

  var deadline = new Date('2026-12-31T23:59:59+05:30').getTime();
  if (Date.now() <= deadline) {
    early.checked = true;
  } else {
    early.checked = false;
    early.disabled = true;
    setText(note, 'The early-bird period ended on 31 December 2026. Standard race fees apply.');
  }

  function update() {
    var fee = FEES[race.value];
    var r = toInt(runners.value);
    var t = toInt(shirts.value);
    var errs = [];
    if (!(r >= 1 && r <= MAX_RUNNERS)) { errs.push('Enter a whole number of runners from 1 to 10.'); }
    if (isNaN(t)) { errs.push('Enter a whole number of T-shirts, 0 or more.'); }
    setText(msg, errs.join(' '));
    if (fee === undefined || errs.length) {
      setText(total, 'Rs --');
      setText(raceAmt, '--');
      setText(shirtAmt, '--');
      if (discRow) { discRow.hidden = true; }
      return;
    }
    var name = race.options[race.selectedIndex].getAttribute('data-name') || 'Race';
    var raceFees = fee * r;
    var discount = (early.checked && !early.disabled) ? Math.round(raceFees / 10) : 0;
    var shirtCost = t * SHIRT;
    var sum = raceFees - discount + shirtCost;
    setText(raceLabel, name + ': ' + r + ' x ' + money(fee));
    setText(raceAmt, money(raceFees));
    if (discRow) { discRow.hidden = discount === 0; }
    setText(discAmt, '- ' + money(discount));
    setText(shirtLabel, 'T-shirts (no discount): ' + t + ' x ' + money(SHIRT));
    setText(shirtAmt, money(shirtCost));
    setText(total, money(sum));
  }

  ['input', 'change'].forEach(function (evt) {
    race.addEventListener(evt, update);
    runners.addEventListener(evt, update);
    shirts.addEventListener(evt, update);
    early.addEventListener(evt, update);
  });
  update();
})();
</script>

<script>
(function () {
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var form = $('reg-form'), dob = $('reg-dob'), race = $('reg-race');
  var yes = $('reg-tshirt-yes'), no = $('reg-tshirt-no');
  var wrap = $('reg-size-wrap'), size = $('reg-size');
  var guardian = $('reg-guardian'), hint = $('reg-guardian-hint');
  var ageMsg = $('reg-age-msg');
  if (!form || !dob || !race || !yes || !no || !wrap || !size || !guardian) { return; }

  var MIN_AGE = { '5K': 12, '10K': 16, 'Half Marathon': 18 };

  function pad(n) { return n < 10 ? '0' + n : String(n); }
  var now = new Date();
  dob.setAttribute('max', now.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(now.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(now.getDate()));

  function ageOnRaceDay(v) {
    var p = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(v || '');
    if (!p) { return NaN; }
    var y = parseInt(p[1], 10), m = parseInt(p[2], 10), d = parseInt(p[3], 10);
    var age = 2027 - y;
    if (m > 2 || (m === 2 && d > 14)) { age--; }
    return age;
  }

  function updateSize() {
    var on = yes.checked;
    wrap.hidden = !on;
    size.disabled = !on;
    size.required = on;
    if (!on) { size.value = ''; }
  }

  function updateAge() {
    var age = ageOnRaceDay(dob.value);
    var under18 = !isNaN(age) && age < 18;
    guardian.required = under18;
    if (hint) {
      hint.textContent = under18
        ? 'Required: the runner is under 18 on race day, 14 February 2027.'
        : 'Needed only if the runner is under 18 on race day, 14 February 2027.';
    }
    var min = MIN_AGE[race.value];
    var text = '';
    if (!isNaN(age) && min !== undefined && age < min) {
      text = 'The ' + race.value + ' has a minimum age of ' + min + '. Choose a different race or check the date of birth.';
    }
    dob.setCustomValidity(text);
    if (ageMsg) { ageMsg.textContent = text; }
  }

  yes.addEventListener('change', updateSize);
  no.addEventListener('change', updateSize);
  dob.addEventListener('input', updateAge);
  dob.addEventListener('change', updateAge);
  race.addEventListener('change', updateAge);
  updateSize();
  updateAge();
})();
</script>

  var stateEl = btn ? btn.querySelector('.j2-nav-hc-state') : null;

  function applyContrast(on, save) {
    if (on) { body.classList.add('j2-hc'); } else { body.classList.remove('j2-hc'); }
    if (btn) { btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', on ? 'true' : 'false'); }
    if (stateEl) { stateEl.textContent = on ? 'On' : 'Off'; }
    if (iconEl) { iconEl.innerHTML = on ? '●' : '◐'; }
    if (save) {
      try { window.localStorage.setItem(KEY, on ? '1' : '0'); } catch (e) { /* storage not available */ }
    }
  }
  var saved = null;
  try { saved = window.localStorage.getItem(KEY); } catch (e) { saved = null; }
  applyContrast(saved === '1', false);
  if (btn) {
    btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
      applyContrast(!body.classList.contains('j2-hc'), true);
    });
  }

  /* Current-section highlight */
  var items = [];
  links.forEach(function (a) {
    var href = a.getAttribute('href') || '';
    var el = href.charAt(0) === '#' ? document.getElementById(href.slice(1)) : null;
    if (el) { items.push({ a: a, el: el }); }

    if (!list || list.scrollWidth <= list.clientWidth) { return; }
    var li = a.parentNode;
    var left = li.offsetLeft - (list.clientWidth - li.offsetWidth) / 2;
    if (list.scrollTo) {
      list.scrollTo({ left: left, behavior: reduce ? 'auto' : 'smooth' });
    } else {
      list.scrollLeft = left;
    }

    if (item === active) { return; }
    active = item;
    links.forEach(function (a) {

    });

    if (atBottom && items.length) { current = items[items.length - 1]; }

<!-- PLACEHOLDER written from the J2 page and the J2 flow diagram (docs/j2-flow.jpg). Replace with the official file when it arrives. -->
# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

# Coordination Agent

## System instruction

You are Coordination, the department's operating timetable. Decide which registered and funded workflow is ready, what must happen before it, and how simultaneous work avoids collisions.

You do not allocate budgets, decide the goal, design workflows or judge result quality.

## Scheduling procedure

1. Consider only workflows that are registered and have a valid envelope.
2. Check triggers and dependencies.
3. Check locks, shared writers and incompatible simultaneous actions.
4. Select the next executable workflow using the declared scheduling rule.
5. Record its slot, expected handoffs and blocking dependencies.
6. If it cannot run, use `HOLD` with the exact missing condition.
7. If another ready workflow exists, schedule it instead of blocking the department.

## Executability objection

During J2.e, you may report that a proposed workflow cannot be scheduled because its dependencies, locks, trigger or handoffs are incoherent. This is evidence for the deterministic validator or Adaptation. It is not authority to approve or rewrite the proposal.

## Boundaries

You may not:

- increase an envelope;
- decide that an expensive workflow is not worthwhile;
- resolve a policy conflict;
- modify the workflow steps;
- mark a result correct;
- ask the CEO directly.

## Failure patterns to avoid

- Scheduling an unregistered proposal.
- Treating “highest priority” as permission to violate dependencies.
- Blocking all work because one workflow is held.
- Ordering work without stating the scheduling rule.
- Becoming a project manager who changes scope.

You are Coordination.

## Reply format (required)
{"say": str, "rule": str, "order": [workflow id], "holds": [{"id": str, "missing": str}], "next": "Priority|Adaptation" (Priority to check the run envelope of the first workflow in your order; Adaptation only if everything is on HOLD), "reason": str (one short sentence: why you decided this)}

[1] Requester (you): Make a website for Riverside Run 2027, a city running event in Pune. Runners should be able to compare the three races, work out what they will pay with a fee calculator, register with a form, see the race-day and expo-day schedule, see the route and water stations for each race, read FAQs, and see sponsors by tier. Volunteers should be able to sign up with a separate form. Add a countdown to race day, a menu that stays on screen and shows which section you are in, and a high-contrast mode that works across the whole page. It should feel sporty and clear and work well on phones.
  Race day: Sunday 14 February 2027. Expo day: Saturday 13 February 2027, 10am to 6pm, at Riverside Grounds, 5 River Road, Pune 411001. Races: 5K (start 7:30am, fee Rs 300, minimum age 12, cutoff 1 hour); 10K (start 6:45am, fee Rs 500, minimum age 16, cutoff 2 hours); Half Marathon (start 6:00am, fee Rs 800, minimum age 18, cutoff 3 hours 30 minutes). Event T-shirt: Rs 250 each, optional. Early-bird: 10% off race fees only (not T-shirts) for registrations up to 31 December 2026. Fee calculator: choose race, number of runners (1 to 10) and number of T-shirts; show the total. Water stations: 5K at 2.5 km; 10K at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 km; Half Marathon every 3 km. Use a placeholder for each route map. Registration form: name, email, phone, date of birth, race (dropdown), T-shirt yes/no, T-shirt size (only shown if T-shirt is yes), emergency contact name and phone, guardian name (only required if the runner is under 18); sends to run@example.com. Volunteer form: name, email, preferred role (Water station, Registration desk, Route marshal), available Saturday / Sunday / both; sends to volunteers@example.com. Schedule: Expo day 10am bib collection opens, 4pm route briefing, 6pm expo closes. Race day 5:00am gates open, 6:00am Half Marathon, 6:45am 10K, 7:30am 5K, 10:00am prize ceremony. FAQs: Can I change my race? Yes, until 31 January 2027 by email. Is there parking? Yes, free at Gate 2. Are refunds available? No. Where do I collect my bib? At the expo on 13 February. Is there a bag drop? Yes, near the start line. Are pacers provided? Yes, for the 10K and Half Marathon. Sponsors: Gold: Meridian Bank; Silver: Trailhead Sports, Aqua Pure; Community: Pune Runners Club. Contact: run@example.com, WhatsApp +91 00000 44444. No photos yet, use placeholders. We are offering S, M, L and XL.

# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

[1] Requester (you): Make a website for Riverside Run 2027, a city running event in Pune. Runners should be able to compare the three races, work out what they will pay with a fee calculator, register with a form, see the race-day and expo-day schedule, see the route and water stations for each race, read FAQs, and see sponsors by tier. Volunteers should be able to sign up with a separate form. Add a countdown to race day, a menu that stays on screen and shows which section you are in, and a high-contrast mode that works across the whole page. It should feel sporty and clear and work well on phones.
  Race day: Sunday 14 February 2027. Expo day: Saturday 13 February 2027, 10am to 6pm, at Riverside Grounds, 5 River Road, Pune 411001. Races: 5K (start 7:30am, fee Rs 300, minimum age 12, cutoff 1 hour); 10K (start 6:45am, fee Rs 500, minimum age 16, cutoff 2 hours); Half Marathon (start 6:00am, fee Rs 800, minimum age 18, cutoff 3 hours 30 minutes). Event T-shirt: Rs 250 each, optional. Early-bird: 10% off race fees only (not T-shirts) for registrations up to 31 December 2026. Fee calculator: choose race, number of runners (1 to 10) and number of T-shirts; show the total. Water stations: 5K at 2.5 km; 10K at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 km; Half Marathon every 3 km. Use a placeholder for each route map. Registration form: name, email, phone, date of birth, race (dropdown), T-shirt yes/no, T-shirt size (only shown if T-shirt is yes), emergency contact name and phone, guardian name (only required if the runner is under 18); sends to run@example.com. Volunteer form: name, email, preferred role (Water station, Registration desk, Route marshal), available Saturday / Sunday / both; sends to volunteers@example.com. Schedule: Expo day 10am bib collection opens, 4pm route briefing, 6pm expo closes. Race day 5:00am gates open, 6:00am Half Marathon, 6:45am 10K, 7:30am 5K, 10:00am prize ceremony. FAQs: Can I change my race? Yes, until 31 January 2027 by email. Is there parking? Yes, free at Gate 2. Are refunds available? No. Where do I collect my bib? At the expo on 13 February. Is there a bag drop? Yes, near the start line. Are pacers provided? Yes, for the 10K and Half Marathon. (function () {
  var FEES = { '5k': 300, '10k': 500, 'half': 800 };
  var SHIRT = 250;
  var MAX_RUNNERS = 10;

  var early = $('calc-early'), total = $('calc-total'), msg = $('calc-msg'), note = $('calc-early-note');

  var discRow = $('calc-disc-row'), discAmt = $('calc-disc-amt');
  var shirtLabel = $('calc-shirt-label'), shirtAmt = $('calc-shirt-amt');
  if (!race || !runners || !shirts || !early || !total) { return; }

  function money(n) { return 'Rs ' + n.toLocaleString('en-IN'); }
  function toInt(v) {
    var s = String(v).replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, '');
    return /^\d+$/.test(s) ? parseInt(s, 10) : NaN;
  }
  function setText(el, t) { if (el) { el.textContent = t; } }

  var deadline = new Date('2026-12-31T23:59:59+05:30').getTime();
  if (Date.now() <= deadline) {
    early.checked = true;
  } else {
    early.checked = false;
    early.disabled = true;
    setText(note, 'The early-bird period ended on 31 December 2026. Standard race fees apply.');
  }

  function update() {
    var fee = FEES[race.value];
    var r = toInt(runners.value);
    var t = toInt(shirts.value);
    var errs = [];
    if (!(r >= 1 && r <= MAX_RUNNERS)) { errs.push('Enter a whole number of runners from 1 to 10.'); }
    if (isNaN(t)) { errs.push('Enter a whole number of T-shirts, 0 or more.'); }
    setText(msg, errs.join(' '));
    if (fee === undefined || errs.length) {
      setText(total, 'Rs --');
      setText(raceAmt, '--');
      setText(shirtAmt, '--');
      if (discRow) { discRow.hidden = true; }
      return;
    }
    var name = race.options[race.selectedIndex].getAttribute('data-name') || 'Race';
    var raceFees = fee * r;
    var discount = (early.checked && !early.disabled) ? Math.round(raceFees / 10) : 0;
    var shirtCost = t * SHIRT;
    var sum = raceFees - discount + shirtCost;
    setText(raceLabel, name + ': ' + r + ' x ' + money(fee));
    setText(raceAmt, money(raceFees));
    if (discRow) { discRow.hidden = discount === 0; }
    setText(discAmt, '- ' + money(discount));
    setText(shirtLabel, 'T-shirts (no discount): ' + t + ' x ' + money(SHIRT));
    setText(shirtAmt, money(shirtCost));
    setText(total, money(sum));
  }

  ['input', 'change'].forEach(function (evt) {
    race.addEventListener(evt, update);
    runners.addEventListener(evt, update);
    shirts.addEventListener(evt, update);
    early.addEventListener(evt, update);
  });

<section id="calculator" class="j2-rc-calc" aria-labelledby="calc-title">
<h2 id="calc-title">Fee calculator</h2>
<p class="j2-rc-lead">Choose a race, the number of runners and the number of T-shirts. The total updates as you go.</p>
<div class="j2-rc-layout">
  <div class="j2-rc-panel" role="group" aria-labelledby="calc-title">
    <label for="calc-race">Race</label>
    <select id="calc-race">
      <option value="5k" data-name="5K" selected>5K (Rs 300)</option>
      <option value="10k" data-name="10K">10K (Rs 500)</option>
      <option value="half" data-name="Half Marathon">Half Marathon (Rs 800)</option>
    </select>
    <label for="calc-runners">Number of runners (1 to 10)</label>
    <input id="calc-runners" type="number" inputmode="numeric" min="1" max="10" step="1" value="1">
    <label for="calc-shirts">Number of T-shirts (Rs 250 each, optional)</label>
    <input id="calc-shirts" type="number" inputmode="numeric" min="0" step="1" value="0">
    <label class="j2-rc-early" for="calc-early">
      <input id="calc-early" type="checkbox">
      <span>Early-bird: registering on or before 31 December 2026</span>
    </label>
    <p class="j2-rc-note" id="calc-early-note">Early-bird applies up to 31 December 2026: 10% off race fees only, never on T-shirts.</p>
    <p class="j2-rc-msg" id="calc-msg" role="alert"></p>
  </div>
  <div class="j2-rc-result" aria-live="polite">
    <h3>Your cost</h3>
    <dl class="j2-rc-rows">
      <div class="j2-rc-row"><dt id="calc-race-label">Race fees</dt><dd id="calc-race-amt">Rs 300</dd></div>
      <div class="j2-rc-row" id="calc-disc-row" hidden><dt>Early-bird 10% off race fees</dt><dd id="calc-disc-amt">- Rs 0</dd></div>
      <div class="j2-rc-row"><dt id="calc-shirt-label">T-shirts (no discount)</dt><dd id="calc-shirt-amt">Rs 0</dd></div>
    </dl>
    <p class="j2-rc-total-label">Total</p>
    <output id="calc-total" class="j2-rc-total" for="calc-race calc-runners calc-shirts calc-early">Rs 300</output>
    <a class="j2-btn j2-btn-secondary" href="#register">Continue to registration</a>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var FEES = { '5k': 300, '10k': 500, 'half': 800 };
  var SHIRT = 250;
  var MAX_RUNNERS = 10;
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var race = $('calc-race'), runners = $('calc-runners'), shirts = $('calc-shirts');
  var early = $('calc-early'), total = $('calc-total'), msg = $('calc-msg'), note = $('calc-early-note');
  var raceLabel = $('calc-race-label'), raceAmt = $('calc-race-amt');
  var discRow = $('calc-disc-row'), discAmt = $('calc-disc-amt');
  var shirtLabel = $('calc-shirt-label'), shirtAmt = $('calc-shirt-amt');
  if (!race || !runners || !shirts || !early || !total) { return; }

  function money(n) { return 'Rs ' + n.toLocaleString('en-IN'); }
  function toInt(v) {
    var s = String(v).replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, '');
    return /^\d+$/.test(s) ? parseInt(s, 10) : NaN;
  }
  function setText(el, t) { if (el) { el.textContent = t; } }

  var deadline = new Date('2026-12-31T23:59:59+05:30').getTime();
  if (Date.now() <= deadline) {
    early.checked = true;
  } else {
    early.checked = false;
    early.disabled = true;
    setText(note, 'The early-bird period ended on 31 December 2026. Standard race fees apply.');
  }

  function update() {
    var fee = FEES[race.value];
    var r = toInt(runners.value);
    var t = toInt(shirts.value);
    var errs = [];
    if (!(r >= 1 && r <= MAX_RUNNERS)) { errs.push('Enter a whole number of runners from 1 to 10.'); }
    if (isNaN(t)) { errs.push('Enter a whole number of T-shirts, 0 or more.'); }
    setText(msg, errs.join(' '));
    if (fee === undefined || errs.length) {
      setText(total, 'Rs --');
      setText(raceAmt, '--');
      setText(shirtAmt, '--');
      if (discRow) { discRow.hidden = true; }
      return;
    }
    var name = race.options[race.selectedIndex].getAttribute('data-name') || 'Race';
    var raceFees = fee * r;
    var discount = (early.checked && !early.disabled) ? Math.round(raceFees / 10) : 0;
    var shirtCost = t * SHIRT;
    var sum = raceFees - discount + shirtCost;
    setText(raceLabel, name + ': ' + r + ' x ' + money(fee));
    setText(raceAmt, money(raceFees));
    if (discRow) { discRow.hidden = discount === 0; }
    setText(discAmt, '- ' + money(discount));
    setText(shirtLabel, 'T-shirts (no discount): ' + t + ' x ' + money(SHIRT));
    setText(shirtAmt, money(shirtCost));
    setText(total, money(sum));
  }

  ['input', 'change'].forEach(function (evt) {
    race.addEventListener(evt, update);
    runners.addEventListener(evt, update);
    shirts.addEventListener(evt, update);
    early.addEventListener(evt, update);
  });
  update();
})();
</script>

<script>
(function () {
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var form = $('reg-form'), dob = $('reg-dob'), race = $('reg-race');
  var yes = $('reg-tshirt-yes'), no = $('reg-tshirt-no');
  var wrap = $('reg-size-wrap'), size = $('reg-size');
  var guardian = $('reg-guardian'), hint = $('reg-guardian-hint');
  var ageMsg = $('reg-age-msg');
  if (!form || !dob || !race || !yes || !no || !wrap || !size || !guardian) { return; }

  var MIN_AGE = { '5K': 12, '10K': 16, 'Half Marathon': 18 };

  function pad(n) { return n < 10 ? '0' + n : String(n); }
  var now = new Date();
  dob.setAttribute('max', now.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(now.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(now.getDate()));

  function ageOnRaceDay(v) {
    var p = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(v || '');
    if (!p) { return NaN; }
    var y = parseInt(p[1], 10), m = parseInt(p[2], 10), d = parseInt(p[3], 10);
    var age = 2027 - y;
    if (m > 2 || (m === 2 && d > 14)) { age--; }
    return age;
  }

  function updateSize() {
    var on = yes.checked;
    wrap.hidden = !on;
    size.disabled = !on;
    size.required = on;
    if (!on) { size.value = ''; }
  }

  function updateAge() {
    var age = ageOnRaceDay(dob.value);
    var under18 = !isNaN(age) && age < 18;
    guardian.required = under18;
    if (hint) {
      hint.textContent = under18
        ? 'Required: the runner is under 18 on race day, 14 February 2027.'
        : 'Needed only if the runner is under 18 on race day, 14 February 2027.';
    }
    var min = MIN_AGE[race.value];
    var text = '';
    if (!isNaN(age) && min !== undefined && age < min) {
      text = 'The ' + race.value + ' has a minimum age of ' + min + '. Choose a different race or check the date of birth.';
    }
    dob.setCustomValidity(text);
    if (ageMsg) { ageMsg.textContent = text; }
  }

  yes.addEventListener('change', updateSize);
  no.addEventListener('change', updateSize);
  dob.addEventListener('input', updateAge);
  dob.addEventListener('change', updateAge);
  race.addEventListener('change', updateAge);
  updateSize();
  updateAge();
})();
</script>

  var btn = document.getElementById('contrast-toggle');

  var KEY = 'j2-high-contrast';
  var reduce = !!(window.matchMedia && window.matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)').matches);

  /* Keep page content clear of the fixed bar */
  function setNavHeight() {
    root.style.setProperty('--j2-nav-h', nav.offsetHeight + 'px');
  }

  /* High-contrast toggle: one class on body switches every colour variable */
  var stateEl = btn ? btn.querySelector('.j2-nav-hc-state') : null;
  var iconEl = btn ? btn.querySelector('.j2-nav-hc-icon') : null;
  function applyContrast(on, save) {
    if (on) { body.classList.add('j2-hc'); } else { body.classList.remove('j2-hc'); }
    if (btn) { btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', on ? 'true' : 'false'); }
    if (stateEl) { stateEl.textContent = on ? 'On' : 'Off'; }
    if (iconEl) { iconEl.innerHTML = on ? '●' : '◐'; }
    if (save) {
      try { window.localStorage.setItem(KEY, on ? '1' : '0'); } catch (e) { /* storage not available */ }
    }
  }
  var saved = null;
  try { saved = window.localStorage.getItem(KEY); } catch (e) { saved = null; }
  applyContrast(saved === '1', false);
  if (btn) {
    btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
      applyContrast(!body.classList.contains('j2-hc'), true);
    });
  }

  /* Current-section highlight */
  var items = [];
  links.forEach(function (a) {
    var href = a.getAttribute('href') || '';
    var el = href.charAt(0) === '#' ? document.getElementById(href.slice(1)) : null;
    if (el) { items.push({ a: a, el: el }); }
  });
  var active = null;

  function reveal(a) {
    if (!list || list.scrollWidth <= list.clientWidth) { return; }
    var li = a.parentNode;
    var left = li.offsetLeft - (list.clientWidth - li.offsetWidth) / 2;
    if (list.scrollTo) {
      list.scrollTo({ left: left, behavior: reduce ? 'auto' : 'smooth' });
    } else {
      list.scrollLeft = left;
    }
  }

  function setActive(item) {
    if (item === active) { return; }
    active = item;
    links.forEach(function (a) {
      a.classList.remove('j2-active');
      a.removeAttribute('aria-current');
    });
    if (item) {
      item.a.classList.add('j2-active');
      item.a.setAttribute('aria-current', 'true');

    items.forEach(function (item) {

    });
    var atBottom = window.innerHeight + (window.pageYOffset || root.scrollTop) >= root.scrollHeight - 2;
    if (atBottom && items.length) { current = items[items.length - 1]; }

# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If

# Audit Agent

## System instruction

You are Audit, the department's independent second pair of eyes. Evaluate observable results against the charter, workflow completion check, rules and source evidence.

You do not design the workflow, repair the result, assign resources, schedule rework or decide policy. Your job is to make discrepancies visible with evidence.

## Finding format

```yaml
finding:
  id: stable identifier
  subject: exact result or claim checked
  criterion: charter, rule or completion-check reference
  evidence: direct observation or source reference
  verdict: PASS | PASS_WITH_WARNING | NEEDS_REVISION | BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE | POLICY_CONCERN
  severity: low | medium | high | critical
  confidence: low | medium | high
  consequence: what is affected
```

## Audit procedure

1. Read the result directly, not only the producing agent's report.
2. Run mechanical checks first.
3. Check each material claim against available evidence.
4. Compare the outcome with the declared completion check and relevant charter clauses.
5. File one finding per distinct issue.
6. Send policy concerns to Identity and correctable defects to Adaptation.
7. Use `BLOCKED_BY_EVIDENCE` when evidence is absent; do not guess.

## J2.e boundary

Do not pre-approve a proposed workflow merely because you could imagine auditing its output. Mechanical workflow validation belongs to the simulator. You may advise whether its completion check is auditable, but you cannot register it.

## Failure patterns to avoid

- Rewriting the work while auditing it.
- Treating stylistic preference as failure.
- Inventing evidence.
- Reporting a score without naming the failed criterion.
- Allowing prior participation in a discussion to bias the verdict.

You are Audit.

<h2 id="calc-title">Fee calculator</h2>
<p class="j2-rc-lead">Choose a race, the number of runners and the number of T-shirts. Leave the T-shirt box empty if you do not want one. The total updates as you go.</p>
<div class="j2-rc-layout">
  <div class="j2-rc-panel" role="group" aria-labelledby="calc-title">
    <label for="calc-race">Race</label>
    <select id="calc-race">
      <option value="" selected>Choose a race</option>
      <option value="5k" data-name="5K">5K (Rs 300)</option>
      <option value="10k" data-name="10K">10K (Rs 500)</option>
      <option value="half" data-name="Half Marathon">Half Marathon (Rs 800)</option>
    </select>
    <label for="calc-runners">Number of runners (1 to 10)</label>
    <input id="calc-runners" type="number" inputmode="numeric" min="1" max="10" step="1" value="1">
    <label for="calc-shirts">Number of T-shirts (Rs 250 each, optional)</label>
    <input id="calc-shirts" type="number" inputmode="numeric" step="1">
    <label class="j2-rc-early" for="calc-early">
      <input id="calc-early" type="checkbox">
      <span>Early-bird: registering on or before 31 December 2026</span>
    </label>
    <p class="j2-rc-note" id="calc-early-note">Early-bird applies up to 31 December 2026: 10% off race fees only, never on T-shirts.</p>
    <p class="j2-rc-msg" id="calc-msg" role="alert"></p>
  </div>
  <div class="j2-rc-result" aria-live="polite">
    <h3>Your cost</h3>
    <dl class="j2-rc-rows">
      <div class="j2-rc-row"><dt id="calc-race-label">Race fees</dt><dd id="calc-race-amt">--</dd></div>
      <div class="j2-rc-row" id="calc-disc-row" hidden><dt>Early-bird 10% off race fees</dt><dd id="calc-disc-amt">--</dd></div>
      <div class="j2-rc-row"><dt id="calc-shirt-label">T-shirts (no discount)</dt><dd id="calc-shirt-amt">--</dd></div>
    </dl>
    <p class="j2-rc-total-label">Total</p>
    <output id="calc-total" class="j2-rc-total" for="calc-race calc-runners calc-shirts calc-early">--</output>
    <a class="j2-btn j2-btn-secondary" href="#register">Continue to registration</a>
  </div>
</div>
<script>
(function () {
  var FEES = { '5k': 300, '10k': 500, 'half': 800 };
  var SHIRT = 250;
  var MAX_RUNNERS = 10;
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var race = $('calc-race'), runners = $('calc-runners'), shirts = $('calc-shirts');
  var early = $('calc-early'), total = $('calc-total'), msg = $('calc-msg'), note = $('calc-early-note');
  var raceLabel = $('calc-race-label'), raceAmt = $('calc-race-amt');
  var discRow = $('calc-disc-row'), discAmt = $('calc-disc-amt');
  var shirtLabel = $('calc-shirt-label'), shirtAmt = $('calc-shirt-amt');
  if (!race || !runners || !shirts || !early || !total) { return; }

  function money(n) { return 'Rs ' + n.toLocaleString('en-IN'); }
  function toInt(v) {
    var s = String(v).replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, '');
    return /^\d+$/.test(s) ? parseInt(s, 10) : NaN;
  }
  /* Empty, negative or unreadable T-shirt entry counts as no T-shirts */
  function shirtCount(v) {
    var s = String(v).replace(/^\s+|\s+$/g, '');
    if (!s) { return NaN; }
    var n = Number(s);
    if (!isFinite(n) || n < 1) { return NaN; }
    return Math.floor(n);
  }
  function setText(el, t) { if (el) { el.textContent = t; } }

  var deadline = new Date('2026-12-31T23:59:59+05:30').getTime();
  if (Date.now() <= deadline) {
    early.checked = true;
  } else {
    early.checked = false;
    early.disabled = true;
    setText(note, 'The early-bird period ended on 31 December 2026. Standard race fees apply.');
  }

  function clearRows() {
    setText(total, '--');
    setText(raceLabel, 'Race fees');
    setText(raceAmt, '--');
    setText(shirtLabel, 'T-shirts (no discount)');
    setText(shirtAmt, '--');
    if (discRow) { discRow.hidden = true; }
  }

  function update() {
    var fee = FEES[race.value];
    var r = toInt(runners.value);
    var n = shirtCount(shirts.value);
    var hasShirts = !isNaN(n);
    var runnersOk = r >= 1 && r <= MAX_RUNNERS;
    setText(msg, runnersOk ? '' : 'Enter a whole number of runners from 1 to 10.');
    if (fee === undefined || !runnersOk) {
      clearRows();
      return;
    }
    var name = race.options[race.selectedIndex].getAttribute('data-name') || 'Race';
    var raceFees = fee * r;
    var discount = (early.checked && !early.disabled) ? Math.round(raceFees / 10) : 0;
    var shirtCost = hasShirts ? n * SHIRT : 0;
    var sum = raceFees - discount + shirtCost;
    setText(raceLabel, name + ': ' + r + ' x ' + money(fee));
    setText(raceAmt, money(raceFees));
    if (discRow) { discRow.hidden = !discount; }
    setText(discAmt, discount ? '- ' + money(discount) : '--');
    if (hasShirts) {
      setText(shirtLabel, 'T-shirts (no discount): ' + n + ' x ' + money(SHIRT));
      setText(shirtAmt, money(shirtCost));
    } else {
      setText(shirtLabel, 'T-shirts (no discount)');
      setText(shirtAmt, 'None');
    }
    setText(total, money(sum));
  }

  ['input', 'change'].forEach(function (evt) {
    race.addEventListener(evt, update);
    runners.addEventListener(evt, update);
    shirts.addEventListener(evt, update);
    early.addEventListener(evt, update);
  });
  update();
})();
</script>

<script>
(function () {
  var $ = function (id) { return document.getElementById(id); };
  var form = $('reg-form'), dob = $('reg-dob'), race = $('reg-race');
  var yes = $('reg-tshirt-yes'), no = $('reg-tshirt-no');
  var wrap = $('reg-size-wrap'), size = $('reg-size');
  var guardian = $('reg-guardian'), hint = $('reg-guardian-hint');
  var ageMsg = $('reg-age-msg');
  if (!form || !dob || !race || !yes || !no || !wrap || !size || !guardian) { return; }

  var MIN_AGE = { '5K': 12, '10K': 16, 'Half Marathon': 18 };

  function pad(n) { return n < 10 ? '0' + n : String(n); }
  var now = new Date();
  dob.setAttribute('max', now.getFullYear() + '-' + pad(now.getMonth() + 1) + '-' + pad(now.getDate()));

  function ageOnRaceDay(v) {
    var p = /^(\d{4})-(\d{2})-(\d{2})$/.exec(v || '');
    if (!p) { return NaN; }
    var y = parseInt(p[1], 10), m = parseInt(p[2], 10), d = parseInt(p[3], 10);
    var age = 2027 - y;
    if (m > 2 || (m === 2 && d > 14)) { age--; }
    return age;
  }

  function updateSize() {
    var on = yes.checked;
    wrap.hidden = !on;
    size.disabled = !on;
    size.required = on;
    if (!on) { size.value = ''; }
  }

  function updateAge() {
    var age = ageOnRaceDay(dob.value);
    var under18 = !isNaN(age) && age < 18;
    guardian.required = under18;
    if (hint) {
      hint.textContent = under18
        ? 'Required: the runner is under 18 on race day, 14 February 2027.'
        : 'Needed only if the runner is under 18 on race day, 14 February 2027.';
    }
    var min = MIN_AGE[race.value];
    var text = '';
    if (!isNaN(age) && min !== undefined && age < min) {
      text = 'The ' + race.value + ' has a minimum age of ' + min + '. Choose a different race or check the date of birth.';
    }
    dob.setCustomValidity(text);
    if (ageMsg) { ageMsg.textContent = text; }
  }

  yes.addEventListener('change', updateSize);
  no.addEventListener('change', updateSize);
  dob.addEventListener('input', updateAge);
  dob.addEventListener('change', updateAge);
  race.addEventListener('change', updateAge);
  updateSize();
  updateAge();
})();
</script>

# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

# Identity Agent

## System instruction

You are Identity, the department's voice and constitutional authority. Keep the department aligned with its goal, done-when condition, rules and authority boundary.

You do not design workflows, allocate resources, schedule work, execute work or perform Audit. You rule only when a proposal touches policy, when Priority and Adaptation cannot agree, when Audit reports a material violation, or when the department may be done.

## Your decisions

You may:

- rule that a proposal is consistent or inconsistent with the charter;
- resolve a bounded Adaptation–Priority conflict;
- interpret an existing rule;
- stop an unsafe or unauthorized action;
- decide whether a material Audit finding requires rework;
- declare that done-when holds when supported by evidence;
- ask the CEO one decision-ready question when existing authority is insufficient.

You may not:

- invent a new goal or rule;
- choose tools or implementation steps;
- increase an envelope;
- choose which workflow runs first;
- rewrite a proposal to make it acceptable;
- ask the CEO merely because agents disagree.

## Decision procedure

1. Name the exact charter clause or rule that applies.
2. Separate facts from assumptions.
3. Decide with existing authority when possible.
4. If the evidence is insufficient but obtainable by another function, request that evidence rather than asking the CEO.
5. Ask the CEO only when the choice changes purpose, risk authority, external commitment or an unresolved value trade-off.

## CEO question format

```yaml
message:
  from: identity
  to: CEO
  act: ASK_CEO
  thread: <thread>
  summary: <one bounded decision>
  claims:
    - "Option A: consequence, cost and risk"
    - "Option B: consequence, cost and risk"
  evidence:
    - <why the charter cannot decide>
  requested_action: "Choose A or B"
  blocking: true
```

## Failure patterns to avoid

- Becoming a general manager who comments on every message.
- Treating personal preference as a rule.
- Escalating without presenting options.
- Silently changing done-when.
- Doing Adaptation's or Audit's work.

You are Identity.

[1] Requester (you): Make a website for Riverside Run 2027, a city running event in Pune. Runners should be able to compare the three races, work out what they will pay with a fee calculator, register with a form, see the race-day and expo-day schedule, see the route and water stations for each race, read FAQs, and see sponsors by tier. Volunteers should be able to sign up with a separate form. Add a countdown to race day, a menu that stays on screen and shows which section you are in, and a high-contrast mode that works across the whole page. It should feel sporty and clear and work well on phones.
  Race day: Sunday 14 February 2027. Expo day: Saturday 13 February 2027, 10am to 6pm, at Riverside Grounds, 5 River Road, Pune 411001. Races: 5K (start 7:30am, fee Rs 300, minimum age 12, cutoff 1 hour); 10K (start 6:45am, fee Rs 500, minimum age 16, cutoff 2 hours); Half Marathon (start 6:00am, fee Rs 800, minimum age 18, cutoff 3 hours 30 minutes). Event T-shirt: Rs 250 each, optional. Early-bird: 10% off race fees only (not T-shirts) for registrations up to 31 December 2026. Fee calculator: choose race, number of runners (1 to 10) and number of T-shirts; show the total. Water stations: 5K at 2.5 km; 10K at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 km; Half Marathon every 3 km. Use a placeholder for each route map. Registration form: name, email, phone, date of birth, race (dropdown), T-shirt yes/no, T-shirt size (only shown if T-shirt is yes), emergency contact name and phone, guardian name (only required if the runner is under 18); sends to run@example.com. Volunteer form: name, email, preferred role (Water station, Registration desk, Route marshal), available Saturday / Sunday / both; sends to volunteers@example.com. Schedule: Expo day 10am bib collection opens, 4pm route briefing, 6pm expo closes. Race day 5:00am gates open, 6:00am Half Marathon, 6:45am 10K, 7:30am 5K, 10:00am prize ceremony. FAQs: Can I change my race? Yes, until 31 January 2027 by email. Is there parking? Yes, free at Gate 2. Are refunds available? No. Where do I collect my bib? At the expo on 13 February. Is there a bag drop? Yes, near the start line. Are pacers provided? Yes, for the 10K and Half Marathon. Sponsors: Gold: Meridian Bank; Silver: Trailhead Sports, Aqua Pure; Community: Pune Runners Club. Contact: run@example.com, WhatsApp +91 00000 44444. No photos yet, use placeholders. We are offering S, M, L and XL.

# Department rules (every function follows these)

You are one of five functions running one department in Native: Identity, Adaptation, Priority,
Coordination and Audit. Each registered workflow gets its own workflow agent ("W-1 Builder", "W-2 Builder", ...)
that runs only that workflow and owns one marked section of the site file. A code validator checks the charter and each
workflow before it is registered. The Requester (a person) gives the brief, answers Identity's questions and
may ask for changes at the end. There is no CEO: where a role file says "ask the CEO", Identity asks the
Requester instead, and no other function may. The department's job right now is to build the website the
Requester asked for.

## How we work
- Everyone reads the whole chat and the current goal before speaking. Keep messages short: 1-3 sentences.
- Address others by @name: @Identity, @Adaptation, @Priority, @Coordination, @Audit, or a workflow agent
  by its id (@W-1).
- Only Identity talks to the Requester (@Requester). If you need something from the Requester, tell
  @Identity; code redirects any other message to the Requester to Identity.
- Identity's goal and "done when" list are the reference for every decision.
- Disagree with a reason tied to the goal, the budget or the standards. Don't give in just to be nice,
  but move when someone gives a better reason.
- Any two functions that disagree (Adaptation and Priority over funding, Adaptation and Audit over a finding,
  Adaptation and Coordination over a HOLD) try to settle it themselves within 4 attempts. If they can't, it
  goes to Identity with both final positions. Identity rules from the charter; if the charter doesn't decide
  it, Identity asks the Requester one decision-ready question, then rules.
- A missing fact only the Requester knows becomes a question from Identity to the Requester. If the Requester
  can't supply it yet, it is "to be confirmed" and that done-when item is not met.
- The work isn't finished until the site is workable: every done-when item passes Audit, no JavaScript
  errors, no horizontal overflow at 360px and 1280px, forms work, no broken in-page link, nothing to be
  confirmed. Until then the loop J2.b to J2.h repeats. When a safety limit is hit (budget, cycles, the same
  failure twice in a row), Identity asks the Requester to add budget, drop the item or ship as is.
- The website is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript in one file (CDN libraries are fine). No build step.

## The flow (J2.a to J2.h)
J2.a Identity: enough information to work? If not, ask the Requester and wait, as many rounds as needed.
Then record the charter. J2.b Adaptation proposes workflows, using relevant lessons from earlier work.
J2.c Priority prices them: GRANT, COUNTER (Adaptation revises) or REFUSE (Adaptation reshapes or parks it);
the bargain is bounded by four hops, fifteen minutes and its spend. J2.d Identity resolves what the agents
couldn't. J2.e The validator checks and registers the workflow and creates its agent (rejected: Adaptation
reshapes or parks it). J2.f Coordination schedules and holds the write lock; Priority checks each run's
envelope (over limit: hold it, or request approval from Identity); the workflow's agent runs it, retrying
within its envelope, and reports to Coordination. J2.g Audit checks the result and files its findings to
Identity. J2.h Identity: is the site workable? If yes, Identity tells the Requester the goal is reached. If
not, back to J2.b. When Audit confirms a fix worked, Adaptation saves a lesson.

## Who speaks next
Every reply names "next". Only these hand-offs are allowed; code redirects any other pick:
- Identity -> Requester, Adaptation, Priority, Coordination or Audit
- Adaptation -> Priority; Identity for a policy question; Audit or Coordination only to dispute a finding or a HOLD
- Priority -> Adaptation; Identity once 4 exchanges are used or to request approval for a run over its envelope;
  the workflow's agent once a run's envelope is within limits; Coordination to HOLD a run
- Coordination -> Priority (envelope check for the next run), Adaptation when everything is on HOLD
- A workflow agent (W-n) -> Coordination
- Audit -> Identity (every finding goes to Identity, who decides J2.h)
Start your message with @<next>.

# Identity Agent

## System instruction

You are Identity, the department's voice and constitutional authority. Keep the department aligned with its goal, done-when condition, rules and authority boundary.

You do not design workflows, allocate resources, schedule work, execute work or perform Audit. You rule only when a proposal touches policy, when Priority and Adaptation cannot agree, when Audit reports a material violation, or when the department may be done.

## Your decisions

You may:

- rule that a proposal is consistent or inconsistent with the charter;
- resolve a bounded Adaptation–Priority conflict;
- interpret an existing rule;
- stop an unsafe or unauthorized action;
- decide whether a material Audit finding requires rework;
- declare that done-when holds when supported by evidence;
- ask the CEO one decision-ready question when existing authority is insufficient.

You may not:

- invent a new goal or rule;
- choose tools or implementation steps;
- increase an envelope;
- choose which workflow runs first;
- rewrite a proposal to make it acceptable;
- ask the CEO merely because agents disagree.

## Decision procedure

1. Name the exact charter clause or rule that applies.
2. Separate facts from assumptions.
3. Decide with existing authority when possible.
4. If the evidence is insufficient but obtainable by another function, request that evidence rather than asking the CEO.
5. Ask the CEO only when the choice changes purpose, risk authority, external commitment or an unresolved value trade-off.

## CEO question format

```yaml
message:
  from: identity
  to: CEO
  act: ASK_CEO
  thread: <thread>
  summary: <one bounded decision>
  claims:
    - "Option A: consequence, cost and risk"
    - "Option B: consequence, cost and risk"
  evidence:
    - <why the charter cannot decide>
  requested_action: "Choose A or B"
  blocking: true
```

## Failure patterns to avoid

- Becoming a general manager who comments on every message.
- Treating personal preference as a rule.
- Escalating without presenting options.
- Silently changing done-when.
- Doing Adaptation's or Audit's work.

You are Identity.

## Reply format (required)

[1] Requester (you): Make a website for Riverside Run 2027, a city running event in Pune. Runners should be able to compare the three races, work out what they will pay with a fee calculator, register with a form, see the race-day and expo-day schedule, see the route and water stations for each race, read FAQs, and see sponsors by tier. Volunteers should be able to sign up with a separate form. Add a countdown to race day, a menu that stays on screen and shows which section you are in, and a high-contrast mode that works across the whole page. It should feel sporty and clear and work well on phones.
  Race day: Sunday 14 February 2027. Expo day: Saturday 13 February 2027, 10am to 6pm, at Riverside Grounds, 5 River Road, Pune 411001. Races: 5K (start 7:30am, fee Rs 300, minimum age 12, cutoff 1 hour); 10K (start 6:45am, fee Rs 500, minimum age 16, cutoff 2 hours); Half Marathon (start 6:00am, fee Rs 800, minimum age 18, cutoff 3 hours 30 minutes). Event T-shirt: Rs 250 each, optional. Early-bird: 10% off race fees only (not T-shirts) for registrations up to 31 December 2026. Fee calculator: choose race, number of runners (1 to 10) and number of T-shirts; show the total. Water stations: 5K at 2.5 km; 10K at 2.5, 5 and 7.5 km; Half Marathon every 3 km.
